utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the butcher shop owned by Alic Kasim?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I remember that Mr. Alic Cazim, not Kasim had a butcher shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was destroyed on the night of the 20th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, it was not destroyed, it was just damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The restaurant owned by Novalic Fevzija, excuse my pronunciation, that was destroyed or damaged on the night of the 20th of January, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I did not get the name. Fevzija Novalic, that is a restaurant, and that restaurant was not destroyed, it was just damaged by the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The kebab shop owned by Dizdarevic Salih, that was destroyed or damaged, wasn't it, on the night of the 20th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with the surname "Salih".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The surname is Judarivic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Salih Dizdarevic you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, I know Salih Dizdarevic, but once again, the kebab shop was not destroyed, it was damaged probably by the bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The gift shop owned by Vensar Tatarevic, was that destroyed or damaged on the night of the 20th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: It was damaged, it was not destroyed. Vensar Tatarevic, I know him. I know the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The business owned by Kerima Nevzudin, was that business destroyed or damaged on the night of the 20th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I think it was damaged. I don't recall the exact date, but I think it was damaged, that this business was damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of these individuals were Muslims, weren't they, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but in addition to those premises, Croatian premises were also damaged by explosives and by shooting. They are premises, businesses next door to each other, and all of them were damaged, but many of these others are not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who carried out this attack on the night of the 20th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Probably by armed criminals or gangs for whatever reasons, out of revolt, revenge and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Armed criminals, Mr. Katava, that UNPROFOR states operated in a pre-planned and coordinated manner against the Muslim population in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I cannot state my opinions as to that, Your Honours. That is UNPROFOR's stand and view. As far as I know, they were settlings of account between the shopkeepers and the war profiteers, because there was a lot of trading going on with goods that were in short supply, and these were sold at astronomically high prices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an atmosphere of terror and fright amongst the Muslim population in Busovaca on the 21st of January, wasn't there, Mr. Katava, and that's why people left, that's why people sent there children away?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was a state of war, and everybody was afraid, the Croats, the Muslims, and we said already that people had sent their wives and children away earlier on, and it is only the military-able men who stayed in Busovaca. So they knew that something was in the making. That's what rumour had. We have an example of this nature too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Katava, please continue.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, I do have an example. I talked to an acquaintance, a Muslim from Busovaca, and he told me, I think that it says so in the documents too, that there were rumours that the Muslims from Krajina would attack Busovaca, and he said, "I sent my wife and children away. I stayed on here and I have a gun, and if necessary I'm going to hand it over, but then I'm afraid there will be an attack."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Judges of this court, Mr. Katava, have heard evidence from Prosecution witnesses that HVO senior civic leaders warned Muslims, senior Muslims in Busovaca, that there was to be an attack by the HVO and that they should leave for their own safety. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I cannot answer that because I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move on to the conflict itself in Busovaca. What date did that take place, the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats in the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I think that this was at the end of January 1993 that military operations started by the Muslim forces against Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that during this attack, 19 Muslim houses in Kadica Strana were torched by HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, during this attack there was a frontline at the Kadica Strana, and they set it up with their own detachment. That was there, and they even had trenches there, and that's where the battle took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question, Mr. Katava. These Judges have heard testimony from witnesses that 19 Muslim houses were torched in Kadica Strana by HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: There were torched houses, Your Honours, at Kadica Strana, but I'm telling you that fighting took place there at that time, and the fact remains that some houses were burned down, and I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it not the case, Mr. Katava, that a large number of Muslim males were imprisoned at the Kaonik military prison after this conflict between the Croats and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, after this conflict and after the cease-fire was brokered, people themselves sought protection. They were simply afraid after the conflict broke out. As the Prosecutor said, they were taken down there for an exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Muslim males were taken to the Kaonik prison facilities after the 26th of January 1993? I think you, yourself, the Judges heard evidence that you, in fact, took somebody to the Kaonik prison facility.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I personally did not take prisoners. And I could not give the exact number, I personally did not take them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many would you say, approximately, how many prisoners, approximately, were kept at the Kaonik prison facility?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I could not exactly say how many there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the figure of 400 be correct, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, I think there were less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More than 300, more than 200?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Around 200, perhaps. I'm not sure. I cannot give you an exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read to you some testimony that the Judges have already heard, and this is Witness Z. Now, are you aware, Mr. Katava, of the murder of Fikret Husanovic, Midhat Hadzibegovic and Nijaz Neslanovic on the 26th of January 1993 by HVO soldiers? INTERPRETER: The interpreters could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Nijaz Neslanovic, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nijaz Neslanovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Midhat Hadzibegovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fikret Husanovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Husanovic? No, I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read to you the testimony of the one survivors from this incident. "Afterwards, when I came to --"

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could we have a page, Counsel?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Afterwards when I came to I called out because the others were dead, and I went to the barn of Salihodzic. I stayed there until the morning. In the morning, around 7.00, I headed towards the police station and I got close to the police when I observed Slavko Katava, a policeman whom I called and asked him whether I may approach. He said I could if I was not armed, so I walked up and he asked what was wrong. I asked him to take me where there were other Muslims and so he took me to Kaonik where almost all detainees were Muslims, and so and I got there." Is that you the Slavko Katava described in this statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: More slowly, please, Mr. Cayley. Repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I won't repeat it all, Mr. President, I'll repeat from halfway through the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In the morning, around 7.00, I headed towards the police station and I got close to the police when I observed Slavko Katava, a policeman whom I called and asked him whether I may approach. He said I could if I was not armed. So I walked up and he asked me what was wrong. I asked him to take me where there were other Muslims, and so he took me to Kaonik where almost all detainees were Muslims, and so, I got there." Now, is this referring to you, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am Slavko Katava, and it is possible that I helped the man, because I helped everyone who addressed me. And perhaps if you would tell me the man's name I would remember. I can't remember. Perhaps I took him to Kaonik, but only if he asked me, but I didn't take anyone ever by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Katava, that Muslim male prisoners at the Kaonik prison were used by the HVO for trench digging purposes?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I don't know about that, because I was not at the Kaonik prison, Your Honour, and I don't know what the organisation was like over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you visit the Kaonik prison?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Perhaps only in such a case, if I drove someone to near the prison of Kaonik, because I didn't go there. Perhaps somebody wanted me to drive him there, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did these several hundred Muslim prisoners go after the agreement of February the 8th, when I think they were released under the control of the International Committee for the Red Cross? Where did these people go?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think they went to the area of Zenica and Kacuni, and I think it was an exchange, and some Croats from the area of Kacuni came to Busovaca, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that prior to January there were two-and-a-half to three thousand Bosniak Muslims living in the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I would agree with you. Your Honour, it was half/half, a bit more Croats in Busovaca, but I would agree it was perhaps half/half, about three-and-a-half thousand people in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three-and-a-half thousand people in the town itself, approximately half of whom were Croat, half were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Half and half, and a bit more Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after April of 1993, how many Muslims were left in the centre of town in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I don't know. Your Honour, I don't know exactly. I know that quite a few families remained. I know that my neighbours stayed on, and I can mention them by name, they are still there; but I cannot give you the exact figures because I didn't pay attention to this. I have my own neighbours, three or four families who live in my apartment building, I know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were about 20 or 30 Muslims left in Busovaca; weren't there, after April of 1993, Mr. Katava? The Judges have already heard testimony to this effect.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there were more than 30 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I do not know the exact number, Your Honour, I already said that. But when I look at my apartment building only, there were three, four families. On average, three members per family, so you can do the mathematics.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, let us go to your report. Could the witness have the exhibit put in front of him, which is now, I think it's Exhibit 450? And if we could look, first of all, at document 96.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first of all, Mr. Katava, the village of Bukovici, was that a mixed village of Muslims and Croats, prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not Bukovici, it is Bukovci, but the majority of the population was Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the village of Grablje, was that a mixed village of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Grablje was a mixed village, Croats, Serbs and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the village of Gusti Grab, was that a mixed village of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, Gusti Grab was a purely Croat village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Javor, was that a mixed village or a purely Croat village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: The village of Javor is a small village and it was only Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: The village of Jelinak is a mixed village, Muslim and Croatian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the village of Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Also mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Krvavicici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Krvavicici is also a small village, only Croats live there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Kula?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: It was a Croatian village, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Milavice?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Also a village with a majority Croat population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Nezirovici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Nezirovici, Your Honour, also a Croat village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Oseliste?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Oseliste, yes, a Croat village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Prosje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Also a Croat village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Putis?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Mixed population, but the majority is Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Muslims and Croats, a mixed village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Solakovici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Also mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Pirici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Pirici, the village of Pirici, that's Croat village, Besici and Turici, that's what it's called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Court when the damage to these buildings, these houses was done in these villages, in what year this occurred?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: As soon as the conflict broke out, Your Honour, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: That's when people were expelled from those houses and they came to the urban area of Busovaca, and we heard them tell us about these houses being destroyed and burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this report it purely concentrates on damage to Croatian property; does it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is a report on damages to Croatian property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you state in the report that the Bosniaks propose in the first stage that people should return to Strane, Loncari, Skradno and Kovacevac. What damage was there to Bosnian Muslim homes in those villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: What were the damages done to -- what was the damage done to Muslim houses, was that the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, the houses were damaged in Loncari, both Croat and Muslim, because this was the frontline, and also the houses in Skradno. Loncari, Jelinak, Putis, all those villages were under Muslim control, and they went back. And now they have returned to Skradno too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's have a look at a map that I've put together, which actually includes -- it is, in fact, on one map so I think it is slightly easier to follow than the Defence exhibit. Mr. Katava, why did you not include in this report the damage to Bosnian Muslim homes in the Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question is not correct, because my learned friend has asked him why he did not enter the damage to Muslim houses, and the witness said that it is a document of the Busovaca municipality, from the head of the municipality, he just recognised it by virtue of its contents and stamp. It is not the witness who drew up the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, this is not the witness's document. Your question isn't properly formulated. You can ask the witness his opinion in a different way. You can't ask him -- well, maybe it's a question of perception.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from what Mr. Nobilo is saying, you cannot state whether the information contained in this report is correct or not, you can only simply identify the stamp of Niko Grubesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I did not say that. I did not say the witness cannot identify it. He confirmed the facts, but he did not compile the document. It was compiled by the municipality, so he doesn't know why only Croat houses were mentioned, but he knows the situation from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the question Mr. Cayley was asking. Further to your objection, Mr. Cayley said that you can only identify it; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, either he knows the contents of this document are true or not. If he doesn't, he shouldn't be here testifying about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. I think that the question has been correctly asked now. Did you understand the question, or do you want the Prosecutor to ask it in a different way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, could he repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is there no mention in this report of the damage done to Bosnian Muslim property? You, yourself, confirmed that 19 houses, Muslim houses in Busovaca were torched, that a number of Muslim businesses were damaged. Why is there no mention of this in this report?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I recognise this document, and I consider that the facts are true. I see that it was signed by Mayor Grubesic, and when asked by the learned counsel, that the Muslims probably compiled similar documents. And so, they were sent to humanitarian organisations and they expressed the need for help and the number of houses damaged. That is my opinion, and I know from practice that that is what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Katava, was the Federation in existence at the time this document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I believe that it existed, Your Honours, but some services were still separate and we still had a parallel administration. They were not all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's correct, isn't it, that this report makes no mention of all of the damage to Bosnian Muslim housing in the municipality of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The question was already asked, you got an answer to that question, Mr. Cayley. Did you give a number to this map?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's 551.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Katava, of the property mentioned in all of these villages, it only refers to Croatian housing in those villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This question has already been answered at least three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear, Mr. Cayley. You can move to another question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Katava, were you in Busovaca throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Throughout the war I was in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I've marked off on here all of the villages that are referred to in this report. In fact, I notice there is one additional that is referred to, Bilalovac, and that is a mistake. But could you go through each of these villages and state to the Judges whether or not these villages were on the line of confrontation between the HVO and Bosnian government forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oseliste?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Oseliste was under the control of the Muslim forces at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know, Mr. Katava, is whether or not it was on a confrontation line, not under whose control it was. Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: The village of Oseliste is on the border of the Kiseljak municipality and follows on from Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Oseliste is a line of confrontation between the HVO and the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: That was not where the front was, Your Honours. The front was at Berstosko, the Defence lines were there between the HVO and the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gusti Grab?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Gusti Grab also it is a village next to Oseliste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Gusti Grab on a frontline position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any fighting in the village of Oseliste between the HVO and the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: There was nobody to fight there in Oseliste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? What do you mean by there was nobody to fight in Oseliste?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, they were repelled by the majority Muslim forces, they didn't have the chance of fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there HVO forces based in Oseliste at any time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I couldn't say, because I wasn't in the village. I know that the people from that village fled to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no idea whether or not there was HVO based in Oseliste, is that what you're stating to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that the people fled in the direction of Kiseljak, that is to say, the locals, the local population of the village of Oseliste, and some of them fell casualty, both women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gusti Grab, were there HVO forces based in Gusti Grab?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, don't change your direction too much. Either you indicate what your objective is and the Judges can follow you with less difficulty, or if you don't want to say where you're going, then ask the same question. Because I'm still thinking about the question about the frontline, and after that when you talk about each village, you go into different analyses, whether it was HVO or something else. So either tell us what you're looking for, that would be clear, and then you can ask all the questions you want, or else remain with the question that you asked, that is, in each of these villages you can ask whether the confrontation line was there. That's to make things clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it is probably important to know the answer to both of those questions; one, whether or not the village was on a confrontation line, and two, whether or not there were HVO forces that were based there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well then, that's clear. And then the witness can try to answer whether in each of the villages the various things happened. Try to answer clearly without many digressions. You know we're going to work today until a quarter to 6.00 because we resumed at a quarter to 3.00. Gusti Grab, Mr. Katava, Gusti Grab, was it on the frontline, and was HVO in it? Please answer.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can show you on the map. You see, the frontline and the delineation between the HVO and the Muslim forces. It was in Donje Polje, and from Donje Polje these places, Kacuni, Gusti Grab, Oseliste and Prosje. That was not controlled by the HVO. So from Donje Polje to Bilalovac, that was under control of the BH army and the frontline was there. If it is easier for me to answer that way, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I suggest that the witness point out Donje Polje so we can all see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The map should be put on the ELMO or -- and on the easel so that the public can witness what's going on. Remember that this is a public hearing. In the second place, in respect of what you asked the witness, I ask that you repeat the question. Put the map either on the ELMO, so it will be on the monitor, or on the easel, in which case the witness would have to get up. And try to go a little bit faster. All right, then on the ELMO. Can the technical booth show it? All right. Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Katava, if we can go through village by village. Gusti Grab, were there HVO forces based in Gusti Grab?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said that in this area -- this area was under the control of the Muslim army, from Donje Polje to Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. You've got your answer. It was the Muslims forces, it wasn't the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to April of 1993, were there HVO forces in Gusti Grab?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: People lived there, Croats lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January of 1993, were there HVO forces based in Gusti Grab?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, after the conflict broke out, the Croats from this area were expelled to Busovaca and all of them left the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please get close -- bring the ELMO closer so the witness can sit down, otherwise, he has difficulty concentrating on his answer. Very well. Mr. Cayley, will you ask your question again? Do you want to move to another village or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there fighting between Muslims and Croats in Gusti Grab?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: There was no fighting, Your Honours, there were just casualties, because the Croats didn't have their units there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Prosje, were there HVO units based there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, there were not in Prosje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Nezirovici, were there HVO units based at any time in that village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The same thing as with the other villages, Nezirovici as well, the people were expelled from there and there were casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No HVO in that village at all, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: There were Croats who were expelled, but there were no HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the village of Turici, were there HVO soldiers ever based in that village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No. The same thing there. All this was under the control of the Muslim army. The HVO soldiers could not have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Milavice at any time were there HVO soldiers based in that village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Milavice are on the confrontation line, the delineation line. Milavice are on the frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the Bosnian army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Between the Muslim forces and the HVO, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Krvavicici, were there HVO units based there prior to January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No. It was a small village and the people had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the village of Javor, were there ever HVO units based in that village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not up there. No one. There were only old men and women there, and they were expelled from up there. This is a very small village above the Muslim villages up there, above Stubice, Sudine, Hozanovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Solakovici, were there ever HVO units based in that village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: The village of Solakovici was also on the defence line, the frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were HVO units based in that village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't understand the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Solakovici.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Solakovici? That is a village on the frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was -- there were HVO units based there and combat took place between the Bosnian army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there weren't any HVO units in Solakovici. Solakovici was under Muslim forces' control, and the frontline was in between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In between where, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Between the Muslim forces and the Croatian defence forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Solakovici was on the confrontation line between HVO forces and Bosnian Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is Donji Solakovici and Gornji Solakovici. Gornji Solakovici was under Bosniak Muslim control, and there were a smaller number of Croatian families there who were expelled to Donji Solakovici. Between Donji Solakovici and Gornji Solakovici there was a line of delineation. I don't know if I've been quite clear now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was an upper Solakovici and a lower Solakovici, and the confrontation line ran through the village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Kula, were there HVO forces based in Kula?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Kula is also on the defence line, on the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were HVO forces based there and combat took place between the HVO and the Bosnian Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Strane, were there HVO forces based in Strane?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did fighting take place there between Bosnian Muslim forces and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Not at Strane Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Grablje, were there HVO forces based in Grablje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No. Grablje was under the control of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Putis, were there HVO forces based in Putis?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Putis, Jelinak and Loncari are villages on the frontline itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the confrontation line between Bosnian Muslim forces and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And fighting took place in those villages between the HVO and the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Katava, you state that you are, I think, a member of the HVO civilian police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Busovaca civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is the name of your father Jozo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were born on the 21st of September, 1956?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, on the 21st of September, 1956 in Donje Polje, municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it not also the case, Mr. Katava, that you have served in the HVO intelligence services, in the SIS? That's the case; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I never served in the SIS. I was a policeman at the Busovaca police station throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the SIS is, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I think those are some kind of intelligence services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Security and information service of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the answer, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Katava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: That is the intelligence service, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you state that you have never served in that organisation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KATAVA
utterances.text: I was never a member of any intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to that point tomorrow. Mr. President, we can pause now and continue with the cross-examination on the balance of the documents tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Not tomorrow morning, it's at 2.00, 2.00 tomorrow. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we please find out from the registrar how long the direct-examination took and how long has the cross-examination taken so far? Perhaps it would be useful to hear this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. There's quite a difference here. Mr. Cayley you have to think that the witness participated in many events, and the Judges want to hear the questions you're asking, but we have to keep a certain balance, a relative balance.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The direct-examination lasted for 30 minutes. I'm not counting the discussions about D450. If I do take that into account, then the direction examination lasted for 1 hour and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying there. It was an hour and 40 minutes or 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Actually, the questions asked took up only 30 minutes, 12 of which were for the projection of the film. But if we count the discussion about the Exhibit 450, that is the document for which there was no translation, then there was 70 minutes of discussion on that. Seventy minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Seventy minutes. In other words, 1 hour and 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That brings us to 1 hour and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Now, this is 105 minutes for the Prosecutor up to this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I can feel that you're going to make an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is a key thing, because procedural questions should not be made at the expense of the direct-examination or the examination as such. If necessary, we are going to make points of order every five minutes. So we should simply see for how long the witness answers the questions of the Prosecutor and how long he answered my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're not going to look at procedure issues. We're simply going to ask Mr. Cayley simply how much longer he needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'll have to look at the documents first, Mr. President, to give an estimate. The only point I would make is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which documents? You know that we said that the first documents are simply documents being filed from A to G, filed the way 456 was filed. We're not going to start that over again. I think that the direct-examination dealt only with the -- J and K. Isn't that right, Mr. Nobilo? As regards the other things, we said that the translations of Tab H should be done. This may mean that the witness has to come back. But as regards documents A through G, in theory, they are being filed the way you filed 456, and you can review them when you like and make any comments you want to make at the proper time, as the Defence did. At least that's what I thought we had decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, my understanding of what was decided, with the deepest of respect, is that in respect of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, when I hear people beginning like that, when I hear, "With all the respect I owe you," I must have made a dreadful mistake. All right. That really worries me. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I would never suggest that you've made a mistake, Mr. President. My interpretation of what you stated was that in respect of Tab H, we would wait until the documents were translated into English, and if necessary, we would exercise our right to request of the Chamber that we bring the witness back to the Court. In respect of documents A to G inclusive, that we would read these documents overnight, and then if we had any questions of the witness we would ask him tomorrow afternoon. We may not have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. That means that the Defence has to go back to its direct-examination. Unless it doesn't want to. But it seems to me that the Defence -- excuse me, Mr. Hayman, I'll talk more slowly. It seems to me that the Defence, on purpose, intentionally, asked no questions about A through G. Was that intentional, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Defence tries to save up time and to bring as many witnesses as possible within a given amount of time. Had we been reading everything with this witness as we did with Slavko Marin, we would have been reading in with him for about seven days. We hope that the relevance of all documents would be understood, and we didn't want to do this through this witness. Mr. Cayley could resort to all the questions he wants to, but within the assigned time. And you saw the cross-examination, and also before that, during the direct-examination, when our time, Defence time, was used on purpose. It is all the same to us what questions are going to be put, but not at the expense of our time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't think that we've understood one another. If you submit the documents A through G and have no question to ask the witness about those documents, we cannot prevent Mr. Cayley from asking questions about documents that you filed covered within A through G. That's what I'm asking you. Was it intentional you did not want to ask any questions about A through G? The registrar is recalling what I said, and I was not wrong. We had authorised the Prosecutor to ask questions about the documents A through G, but insofar as you decided not to ask questions about A through G, I give you back the right to ask them, which means that if the Prosecutor, as it is his intention, wants to ask questions about A through G, because they're here and the witness is here too, at that point, if you like, Mr. Nobilo, tomorrow you can directly examine the witness on the documents A through G, and then there would be cross-examination. But if you waive that right, you waive that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have understood the ruling of the court. With your permission, we would like to think about this until tomorrow. However, the crucial thing is that we do not oppose a single question put by the Prosecutor which is within the scope of the examination-in-chief and within the time that we used. We do not oppose any question. However, it is quite noticeable that every one of our witnesses is examined two or three times longer in cross-examination than during direct-examination. We did not have this opportunity while the Prosecution witnesses were being heard, because we were told that this had to be proportionate in terms of time. I can understand it if it was 15, or 20 or 30 per cent, but every time 200 per cent, 300 per cent more. I mean, in that case, both parties are not equal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. This question -- there were two possible solutions. Let me be very clear, because I have the impression that we aren't being very clear, and perhaps I wasn't clear. We had thought that documents A through G would be filed as the Prosecutor did with 456. I, rather, was inclined to think that the Defence -- that the Defence did not want to ask any questions about those documents. And it is true, at another point in the discussion, which was a long one, we authorised Mr. Cayley to review the documents A through G so that he could cross-examine the witness. But when you questioned your witness, Mr. Nobilo, I noted that you didn't take up very much time, and that you asked questions only about the documents J and K. Therefore, I thought that I would take away the Prosecution's right to cross-examine the witness on those documents, because you had assumed that the documents A through G would in some way be filed with the Tribunal as the Prosecution had done with 456. All this out of a concern for maintaining equilibrium, since the original objection, Mr. Hayman, had to do with the so-called imbalance that the Judges had allowed in terms of 456. Now Mr. Cayley is reminding me and telling me that, of course, at another point we said so long as the witness is here, Mr. Cayley could take advantage of tomorrow morning to study all of the documents, A through G, and then to cross-examine the witness. And if -- I think that it's natural that should you be limited in any way, it would be natural for you to -- for us to give you back the right to ask any questions that you want to ask about A through G. But if you're saying to me that, "All in all we do not intend to ask any questions about A through G," then I will maintain the Prosecutor's right to ask questions, because it was your choice not to ask those questions, or it would be in your choice in any case, but, of course, I will ask the Prosecutor to do it quickly. Is it clear what I've said?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We think it is clear, Mr. President. We think the Prosecutor should have the right to ask questions about categories A through G within the scope and within the time limits set by Your Honour. The Defence's remedy, should that examination be allowed to go on for a long period of time, would be on redirect examination we believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Let me turn to Mr. Cayley, because now the question is clear. You have reviewed the documents A through G, you're going to continue to review them. Can you give us an approximate amount of time it will take you to read them? We can't give you the whole afternoon, that would be difficult, but you can ask the questions you want about them, and then the Defence will decide whether it wants to question the witness. All right, we'll resume tomorrow at 2.00. What do you have, about an hour's worth of questions to ask yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I imagine that that's a fair estimate, Mr. President. I will try and get through it in an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, about an hour. All right. Since you are -- this is not a cross-examination. I turn to Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Hayman. Because you were self-limited by not asking questions about A through G -- Judge Riad is looking at me with a great deal of indulgence I am repeating myself -- you were frustrated, given the fact that the Prosecutor might need an hour for A through G. At 2.00 tomorrow do you want to take advantage of about a half hour, three-quarters of an hour to ask questions about A through G? You are the one who has to decide about this, it's your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, of course we do not waive our right to redirect, and we shall certainly avail ourselves of that right, but we think that the Prosecutor overstepped his time considerably, and we should have, for the redirect, at least as much time as the Prosecutor is going to use up for documents A through G which we did not examine the witness on yesterday, because this is going to be something completely new, something that we hadn't discussed. So if the Prosecutor needs an hour for that, then we need an hour too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's fine. Then you have the redirect time. So you'll have all the time you need, if you agree. Tomorrow -- I turn to my colleagues. Do you agree with me? We will begin at 2.00. If you agree, Mr. Cayley, I won't give you the floor immediately, I'll give it to Mr. Nobilo so he could begin his examination, which will last a half hour, three-quarters of an hour, unless he wants to do it through redirect. Would you rather do it through redirect? All right. That's even easier then. That would make things even easier. All right. Mr. Cayley, tomorrow we will give you the floor at 2.00 for about an hour, about an hour, I say. Then you have redirect time which -- for which time you will not be limited by the Judges. We hope that we'll be able to finish by tomorrow afternoon, because the Judges have some questions that they're going to want to ask also. Have I succeeded in being clear this time? All right. Court stands adjourned and we will resume tomorrow at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
